ms.promise:
Context: zkProver is a backend application. It provides a public API for calculation of zero-knowledge proofs.
Task: We will be implementing the Plonk prover algorithm. The performance-critical operations will be implemented in Rust, while the high-level protocol will be in Haskell.
Outputs:
・Bindings for FFT and multi-scalar multiplication imported from Rust into Haskell
・Plonk prover algorithm (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
・Bindings for FFT and multi-scalar multiplication imported from Rust into Haskell can be found in the repo
・Plonk prover algorithm (Haskell) can be found in the repo
ms.report:
Bindings for FFT and multi-scalar multiplication imported from Rust into Haskell.
The relevant bindings are located here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/tree/main/rust-ffi
You can find the E2E tests here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/tree/main/rust-ffi-test
FFT and MSM are the key performance-critical operations in the most widely used proving algorithms, including Plonk. This part of the project ensures that our solution is competitive in terms of the proving speed.
Plonk prover algorithm. Relevant modules:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/src/ZkFold/Base/Protocol/ARK/Plonk.hs
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/src/ZkFold/Base/Protocol/ARK/Plonk/Internal.hs
A Haskell implementation of the Plonk prover. It is a well-known and a widely used zero knowledge proof protocol. This implementation allows us to implement recursive ZKP protocols in the future which would be of great benefit to DApp developers, especially those who use ZK in the data protection context.
Description of modules:
https://github.com/zkFold/project-catalyst-reports/tree/main/ZK%20Prover%20Backend
On top of that, we have shared the progress via our X account (read the thread): https://twitter.com/zkFold/status/1779819515464888709
Two broken links have been resubmitted.

ms.promise:
Context: zkProver is a backend application. It provides a public API for calculation of zero-knowledge proofs.
Task: We will be implementing the Protostar prover algorithm (API endpoint 2). We will also implement a custom transaction balancing algorithm for zkFold Symbolic smart contracts (API endpoint 3).
Outputs:
・Protostar prover algorithm (Haskell)
・zkFold Symbolic transaction balancing algorithm (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
・Protostar prover algorithm (Haskell) can be found in the repo
・zkFold Symbolic transaction balancing algorithm (Haskell) can be found in the repo
ms.report:
Protostar prover algorithm
The Protostar algorithm implementation is split across several modules, which can be found here (the link has been updated)
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/tree/vks4git/protostar/src/ZkFold/Base/Protocol/Protostar
Description: Protostar folding allows construction of "recursive" arithmetic circuits. These circuits correspond to programs containing loops and recursive function calls. On top of that, it also enables creation of data types with variable byte length which are very common in the Cardano ledger specification. This feature makes our zkFold Symbolic framework much more robust and enables efficient implementation of zero knowledge smart contracts on Cardano.
zkFold Symbolic transaction balancing algorithm
We have also implemented off-chain (transaction balancing) code for zkFold Symbolic smart contracts. One can find the relevant console scripts here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-cardano/tree/main/e2e-test/plonk
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-cardano/tree/main/e2e-test/symbolic
Besides that, the off-chain Haskell code related to the task can be found here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-cardano/tree/main/backends
Description: Currently, we have two types of zkFold Symbolic smart contracts:
・Plonk smart contracts mint a token if and only if a proof verification succeeds

on-chain. The input to the verification algorithm is the token name.
・Symbolic smart contracts succeed if and only if a transaction satisfies a

particular condition encoded as an arithmetic circuit.
Finally, we have published this report on GitHub:
https://github.com/zkFold/project-catalyst-reports/blob/main/ZK%20Prover%20Backend/Milestone%203.pdf
And posted about the milestone on X (we have added two more comments to explain implemented features to the community):
https://x.com/zkFold/status/1823800347980095983

ms.promise:
Context: zkProver is a backend application. It provides a public API for calculation of zero-knowledge proofs.
Task: As proof calculation is computationally expensive, we will implement a load distribution algorithm that splits the proving task between several backend provers running in parallel.
Outputs:
・Modules for load distribution and parallel proof computation on multiple server instances (Haskell)
・Managed API access through the Maestro platform
ms.criteria:
・Modules for load distribution and parallel proof computation on multiple server instances (Haskell) can be found in the repo
・Managed API access through the Maestro platform can be found in the repo
ms.report:
We have completed the Milestone 4 of the project.
To parallelize ZKP computations, we implemented a new version of the accumulator scheme that can be found here:
https://github.com/zkFold/symbolic/blob/vlasin-cyclefold-2/symbolic-base/src/ZkFold/Base/Protocol/IVC/AccumulatorScheme.hs#L159
New algorithm prove' can combine computations performed by independent provers into an aggregated proof.
In addition, the proving server has been updated to use the latest version of symbolic library:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-prover-api
We have updated the instructions to build and deploy the prover on Maestro infrastructure. Test query is provided here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-prover-api/blob/main/README.md?plain=1#L31
Update:
The API endpoint is currently available at
http://54.93.43.251:3001/prove
Example of a correct POST request to the endpoint (using curl):
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '"MA=="' 54.93.43.251:3001/prove
Update 2:
We have added the message returned by the server in response to the sample request above. Here is the link to the message file:
https://github.com/zkFold/project-catalyst-reports/blob/main/ZK%20Prover%20Backend/response.txt
The response contains the encoded proof corresponding to the encoded witness message "MA==". For economic reasons, we hosted the service on a free-tier AWS infrastructure rather than the core Maestro infrastructure. Once there is a demand for this service, the proposers will scale it up and re-host on the core Maestro infrastructure. Thanks for understanding.
